selected_result: Rump Theorem 4.3 and equation (4.2): a computable dot-product absolute-error estimate using the rounded product-absolute-value accumulator, with underflow and sharp coefficient

bibliographic_source.title: Error Estimation of Floating-Point Summation and Dot Product
bibliographic_source.venue: BIT Numerical Mathematics 52 (2012), 201–220; author preprint accepted 2011

paper_locations.anchor: Binary floating-point set F, round-to-nearest, unit roundoff u, underflow unit eta, ufp and realmin
First rounded product initializes dot accumulator; subsequent rounded products are added recursively while their absolute values are summed in parallel

task_clarification: For positive n, x,y ∈ F^n, and (n+2)u ≤ 1, compute each rounded product p_hat_i=fl(x_i*y_i), then the left-to-right dot-product sum s_hat and the concurrent left-to-right sum S_hat of |p_hat_i| exactly as Algorithm 4.2 specifies.

With eta the smallest positive subnormal and realmin=(1/2)u^{-1}eta the smallest positive normal, formalize both strict bounds in (4.2): |s_hat−xᵀy| < (n+2)u·ufp(S_hat)+n*eta/2 < (n+2)u·ufp(S_hat)+realmin.

The labelled theorem also asserts that the factor n+2 cannot be replaced by n+1. Retain the corresponding sharpness/counterexample assertion under its intended format and dimension conditions; if its domain cannot be specified faithfully, exclude this task rather than silently dropping it.
scope_constraints: Do not assume away underflow. Its additive eta and realmin contributions are part of the result.
Preserve the strict inequalities, the exact (n+2) coefficient, the smallness guard, and the rounded rather than exact absolute-product accumulator.
Do not narrow to fixed n, nonnegative inputs, or a no-cancellation case.
Use round-to-nearest binary arithmetic with no overflow as in the source; no hypothesis may itself state the desired estimate.
Algorithm 4.2's first rounded product initializes both accumulators, so an extra rounded zero-addition must not silently change the algorithm.
